subject: Civil Engineering
title: Pavement Distress: Cracks and Potholes
description: Learn Pavement Distress: Cracks and Potholes in one minute.

hook.text: A pothole swallows your tire. That hole started as a tiny crack months ago.

buildup.text: Fatigue cracking starts from repeated truck loads — alligator-pattern cracks spread.

discovery.text: Water enters cracks, freezes, expands, and pops out chunks — a pothole is born.

twist.text: Rutting happens when asphalt deforms under heavy loads in hot weather — permanent grooves.

climax.text: Pavement management systems track every crack and schedule repairs before potholes form.

punchline.text: Fix the crack and you prevent the pothole. Ignore it and you rebuild.

quiz.question: How does water contribute to pothole formation?
options: Water dissolves the asphalt binder chemically
Water enters cracks, freezes and expands, breaking apart the pavement
Water lubricates the road surface causing tires to erode it faster

details.summary: Pavement distresses are visible signs of structural or surface deterioration including fatigue cracking, rutting, potholes, raveling, and joint faulting. Engineers classify and measure distresses using standardized surveys to determine when maintenance, rehabilitation, or reconstruction is needed.
details.whyItMatters: Identifying distresses early enables preventive maintenance that costs a fraction of reconstruction. Pavement management decisions affect billions in annual transportation spending worldwide.
takeaways: Fatigue alligator cracking indicates structural failure in the pavement layers
Potholes form when water enters cracks and weakens underlying material
Regular pavement condition surveys drive cost-effective maintenance timing

faq.question: How do potholes actually form?
faq.answer: Water enters through surface cracks and weakens the base layer. Traffic loads push the weakened material aside, creating a cavity beneath the surface. Eventually the surface layer collapses into the void. Freeze-thaw cycles accelerate the process by expanding water in cracks.

faq.question: What is the difference between structural and functional pavement failure?
faq.answer: Structural failure means the pavement layers cannot support traffic loads, shown by deep cracking and deformation. Functional failure means the surface is too rough or slippery for comfortable safe driving, even if structurally sound. Both require different treatment strategies.
